Variety is literally the spice of life in Andhra cuisine.
The region is traditionally known as the ‘spice heartland of India’, and there is no getting away from the range of fiery masalas - like Guntur Sannam chillies, gongura leaves, turmeric, ginger, and mustard seeds - that add so much ‘oomph’ to Andhra dishes. Chennai has always played host to a large Telugu community from different walks of life, making Andhra cuisine immensely popular in the city for its distinctive spices and traditional recipes. Their hospitality comes alive at some of the city’s iconic eateries. Here is our pick.
The National Lodge
Third-generation family member Satyanarayana Deepak says, “When my grandfather, K Ethiraj established the National Lodge in 1952, it functioned as a lodging house and a restaurant. Businessmen from across the Madras Presidency would come to Sowcarpet for trade. For many, especially those from Andhra, this became the preferred place to stay and enjoy homely Andhra food.” Today, Deepak, along with his brother, Satyanarayana Dwarak and son, Vidhant, manage the Sowcarpet and Mount Road outlets, serving nearly 120 diners at a time.
As with most traditional Andhra cuisine, the meals are the highlight of the day. Once the rice is served, the National special parupu podi arrives, and either raw tamarind chutney, gongura pachadi or tomato thokku are served in turns. The piece-de-resistance arrives with the second serving of rice — a delicious bowl of vada sambar. The leaf is further adorned with poriyal, pickle, pachadi, rasam, buttermilk and finally, curd with sugar! It is evidently, the quality that has sustained them for as long.
Sowcarpet and Anna Salai, Phone: 9840161919.
New Andhra Meals Hotel
Towards the eastern end of Pondy Bazaar, Chennai’s shopping hub, stands the New Andhra Meals Hotel, drawing a steady stream of patrons as well as first time diners who arrive on recommendation.
“We serve the traditional vegetarian meals on the banana leaf, with the option of non-vegetarian side dishes. If requested we also serve non-vegetarian gravies,” says P Balakrishna, the owner, who is known to be at the outlets early each day. The Pondy Bazaar branch has been managed by Venkatesan since 2001, while Balakrishna’s close associate Prakash oversees operations here as well as at the newer Valasaravakkam outlet.
The highlight of their Andhra meals is the generously sized vanjaram fry, along with succulent Andhra prawns, with the fish sourced from a regular vendor in Zam Bazaar. With these two items on the leaf, everything else takes a back seat, though the rest of the fare holds its own. The Nellore rice which is specially sourced, compliments dishes such as karakozhambu, sambar, rasam and morekolambu. “Guntur chicken, Hyderabad chicken 65, mutton and gongura are prepared by using our own spices,” says Balakrishna, adding that their mutton, chicken and egg biryanis are equally popular.
I am told that very little has changed in their menu over the years. “It has always been selectively curated and only the most sought-after dishes are featured,” says Balakrishna. “However, due to popular demand we have introduced tandoori chicken, chapathi and parotta.”
T Nagar, Phone: 7708099915.
Amaravathi, Cathedral Road
At Amaravathi, the second generation, represented by Nivruti Reddy, is a constant presence at the flagship outlet on Cathedral Road, even as she manages her time across other establishments. When I walk into Amaravathi at lunch time, the place is packed. “The sourcing of raw materials and preparation are carefully coordinated, a process refined over the years. Every ingredient is made in-house,” she says, joining me at the table.
Amaravathi is best known for its meals, popular both during lunch and dinner. “Our in-house preparations like rotu pachchadi and ragi ball with Andhra fish pulusu are in constant demand,” says Ramesh, the manager. As the banana leaf is filled with chutneys, pickles, and thokkus, the ragi ball catches my eye. Dipped in the spicy fish curry, it tastes divine.
I wonder if the health conscious diner still indulges in Andhra cuisine. Alongside the traditional vegetarian meals, complimented by non-vegetarian side dishes, the biryani platter is a popular choice. It features four small portions each of mutton, chicken, and prawn biryani along with white rice. Diners can also opt for three non-vegetarain gravies as add-ons. Not to be missed are the highlights — Andhra chicken and vanjaram fry. The meal ends with a delicious tumbler of South Indian coffee. A fitting end.
Mylapore. Phone: 9500020011.
Velidis, Ramapuram
After several years as an advertising professional, V Veeraiah chose to follow a passion and enter the food industry, taking on the responsibility of managing the kitchen of a leading club in the city. “That the speciality of the club was Andhra cuisine was coincidental, given my family background as chilli growers from Chirala,” says Veeraiah.
When an opportunity arose, he decided toopen Velidis (named after his family) in the busy Ramapuram locality in 2004. “That’s when I realised that the area was already crowded with many Andhra messes serving meals for much below ₹100 a plate,” recalls Veeraiah. Undeterred, he curated a distinctive menu of Andhra dishes. Velidis special chicken biryani and Velidis joint chicken biryani, both topped with Megana chicken dry or Aalfa chicken dry are the most popular dishes. “That we source the best quality Guntur chillies and use only basmati rice for our biryanis, has ensured the top quality in taste. For our seafood dishes, fresh vanjaram and prawns are procured daily and we do not refrigerate them for the next day,” informs Veeraiah.
The biryani has a distinct flavour and I am told the dishes are cooked on coal, as are their tandoori preparations. The success of Velidis at Ramapuram has encouraged him to open another outlet in Pallavaram.
Manapakkam. Phone: 9380938513.

Researchers have reviewed 77 meta-analyses spanning 116 different bipolar disorder treatments and identified the most effective ones across age groups and mood phases.
Bipolar disorder is a mental disorder, characterised by extreme swings in mood, energy levels and activity. The disorder can causes phases of depression marked by a low mood and energy or mania, in which mood and activity levels tend to be high.
Researchers, led by those from The Ottawa Hospital in Canada and universities in Spain, Italy, France and the UK, have created EBI-BD (Evidence Based Interventions for Bipolar Disorder).
EBI-BD is an open-access web platform clearly presenting the impact, side effects, and strength of evidence for each treatment based on findings from the "most comprehensive" review, published in The British Medical Journal.
For bipolar depression, effective treatments for adults include cariprazine, fluoxetine and lurasidone, while those among children and teenagers were lurasidone and olanzapine with fluoxetine.
Effective interventions for mania episodes among adults include aripiprazole, haloperidol, lithium and risperidone, whereas those for children and teenagers include aripiprazole, asenapine and olanzapine.
Maintenance dose -- prescribed to prevent future episodes and for long-term health -- effective for adults include aripiprazole, lithium and risperidone.
"We hope clinicians will be able to use the platform with their own patients to find the best balance between efficacy and side effects, according to each patient's needs," author Michele De Prisco, psychiatrist and researcher at the Hospital Clínic de Barcelona and the University of Barcelona, Spain, said.
"Using the platform and its integrated preference tool, clinician and patient can decide together which treatment to consider next," Dr De Prisco said.
Author -- Jess Fiedorowicz, head and chief of mental health at The Ottawa Hospital and professor at the University of Ottawa, said medications for the mental health disorder can come with varied side effects.
"A tool that incorporates patient preferences and promotes shared decision-making can help find treatments that are a better fit," Dr Fiedorowicz said.
Results from the review have also been used to update guidelines, including those of the International Society for Bipolar Disorders (ISBD), for the management of bipolar disorder.
The study is the first living umbrella review to include all treatment strategies assessed across any age group and phase of bipolar disorder from the largest and best meta-analyses available to date, the researchers said.
The review can be adapted rapidly as new evidence emerges and serves as a foundation for continuously improving care, which is why it is called a "living review", they said.
"Living reviews like this one are game-changers when it comes to updating international treatment guidelines," author Samuele Cortese, research professor at the University of Southampton, UK, said.
"Rather than taking a week to get an answer, experts can consult the website in real time during meetings for the latest evidence," Dr Cortese said.
The authors wrote, "The EBI-BD tool can help clinicians make evidence-based, personalised treatment decisions for bipolar disorder."

Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury has written to Chief Minister Revanth Reddy of the Congress-led government in Telangana, asking that the State government take a position in the Supreme Court to support the Constitutional challenges to the recently passed amendments to the Transgender Rights law that removed the right to self-identification of gender identity.
The law, passed in Parliament this March, ran into widespread protests from the transgender community across the country and had also led to resignations from members appointed to the Government’s National Council for Transgender Persons over provisions that mandate medical certification of gender identity instead of relying on self-identification.
Ms. Chowdhury, whose opposition to the amendments has been vocal, inside and outside Parliament, has now asked the Congress government in Telangana to support the challenges to the amendment that are currently being heard in the Supreme Court of India. In a letter to Mr. Reddy, the Congress’ Rajya Sabha MP from Telangana said, “I would earnestly request the Government of Telangana to extend its support to these proceedings through the office of the Learned Additional Advocate General, Shri Rajnikanth Reddy, by assisting the court in defence of the constitutional rights and dignity of transgender persons.”
In addition to this, Ms. Chowdhury has also requested the Telangana government to “carefully examine the administrative, financial and implementation implications of the new Act” for the State. She noted that this was needed to look at where the amended Act “may conflict with the State’s existing welfare architecture and its commitment to protecting the rights of transgender persons”.
Ms. Chowdhury noted in her letter to the Telangana CM that the State has “consistently stood for inclusion, social justice, and constitutional morality, and its intervention at this stage would carry both legal and moral significance.”
She also noted that during the debate on the amendments in Rajya Sabha, the Congress party had strongly opposed the legislation on the grounds that it undermined the principles of dignity, equality, and self-identification recognised by the Supreme Court, and “strikes at the heart of the guarantees under Articles 14, 15, 19, and 21 of our Constitution”.
At the time the Bill was being introduced and discussed, a delegation of trans activists from across the country had also met with the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi and Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in New Delhi, following which the official account of the Indian National Congress had posted a statement saying that Mr. Gandhi reiterated that the “Congress party stands firmly with the rights and dignity of transgender persons and will oppose the Bill in Parliament”.
Soon after the amendments to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act were passed, several challenges to it were filed before the Supreme Court of India, which has issued notice in these matters to the Union government. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for August 17.

Andhra:2018 Andhra Group-I exam riddled with irregularities, say SIT probe
Amaravati, An SIT probing the 2018 Andhra Pradesh Group-I recruitment examination has uncovered alleged irregularities across multiple stages of evaluation, including the use of unauthorised evaluators, purported manual evaluation at a private resort and widespread alterations in OMR evaluation sheets.
The probe pertains to Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission's recruitment of 169 Group- I posts through a notification issued in 2018. It attracted more than 1.14 lakh applications.
"An SIT probing the 2018 Andhra Pradesh Group-I recruitment examination, the state's premier civil services examination has uncovered serious irregularities across multiple stages," said a press release.
The SIT was constituted by the Andhra Pradesh government in February 2026, following directions from the High Court to scientifically examine allegations of tampering and irregularities in the recruitment process.
According to the SIT, alleged irregularities had occurred during three separate evaluation exercises - the original digital valuation in 2021, a purported manual valuation conducted at a private resort following a High Court order, and a second manual valuation conducted at Vijayawada in 2022 during the erstwhile YSRCP government.
During the digital evaluation, the SIT alleged that unauthorised evaluators, private e-mail and mark discrepancies had occurred, adding that the first major irregularities arose during digital evaluation of the mains stage of the examination.
"The SIT found that the decision to introduce digital evaluation, as well as the panel of evaluators engaged for the exercise did not carry the mandatory approval of the PSC Chairman," said the press release.
Out of a secretary-approved panel of 158 evaluators, only 72 actually evaluated the answer scripts while another 25 persons who were not on the approved panel also evaluated answer scripts and were paid, the SIT claimed.
The approved panel itself predominantly consisted of teachers and lecturers from private schools and colleges instead of the university-level subject experts contemplated by the PSC Office Manual, it said.
The digital evaluation was coordinated through an unofficial private e-mail account, personal email accounts and Google Drive links, said the SIT.
The probe noted alleged differences between marks originally entered by the evaluators and the marks reflected in the final digital-result database.
The SIT noted that the second-evaluation marks were allegedly entered in several cases without an independent second examiner, with one freelancer, Mahamkali Raghuram, making such entries himself.
The SIT observed that the PSC paid ₹1.38 crore to Stone Media Advisory Services and TrueGrader for the digital evaluation exercise, adding that Raghuram received approximately ₹10 lakh towards evaluation and coordination work.
Following candidates challenging the digital evaluation in the High Court, it ordered a manual evaluation, observing that the notified methodology to digital valuation was contrary to the recruitment notification.
Later, the SIT noted that manual evaluation was undertaken at a private resort, which was not a government office but a private space, where "manual evaluation" amounted to only allegedly re-entering the earlier digital marks.
According to the SIT, answer scripts had remained in a private agency's custody for 84 days and accused the then PSC secretary PSR Anjaneyulu over the manual evaluation irregularities.
Further, it noted that the second manual evaluation was conducted in Vijayawada after D Gautam Sawang took charge of the PSC in February 2022.
However, the SIT alleged that there was no documentary record supporting the policy decision of the then PSC chairman, Sawang, to conduct the second manual evaluation.
In the second manual evaluation, the SIT claimed that there were several discrepancies, such as alleged 95 percent alterations or over-writings, different inks and handwritings and others.
Highlighting that forensic material was examined by Central Forensic Science Laboratory in Hyderabad, New Delhi, Shimla, Pune, Bhopal, Kolkata and Guwahati, the SIT raised concerns over the custody and surveillance of confidential examination material.
It found that there was allegedly no CCTV coverage over the PSC Confidential Sections or the Strong Room during the original examination period.
"During the fresh manual valuation in 2022, cameras were initially installed only in two confidential-section rooms. The Strong Room itself came under CCTV only on April 11, 2022 17 days after valuation began," said the press release.
Even after cameras were installed, the SIT found multiple alleged inconsistencies between CCTV footage and the official Guard Register.
The SIT additionally found that most examiners were allegedly using mobile phones inside the manual evaluation camps and another inconsistency was the unusually large number of answer scripts that required a third evaluation.
According to PSC, only 0.45 percent of scripts required third evaluation in the previous Group-I recruitment, compared with alleged 10.2 percent in the 2018 recruitment process.
"The SIT said that while this alone could not establish wrongdoing, the dramatic increase, taken together with over-writing, unauthenticated corrections, signature mismatches and other forensic irregularities, indicated serious inconsistency in the evaluation process," the release said.
A criminal case was registered in April 2025 under Sections 409, 477-A, 420 and 120-B read with Section 34 of the IPC.
Camsign Media Director P Madhusudhan Rao was arrested in May 2025, while Anjaneyulu was secured on a Prisoner Transit Warrant for investigation.
The SIT examined 173 witnesses, and the investigation includes forensic reports, financial records, WhatsApp communications, electronic data, valuation records, videos and reconstruction of the evaluation processes at both the resort and Vijayawada.

"Assam and Arunachal Pradesh share a deep bond of history, friendship and brotherhood. Our differences must always be addressed through dialogue, mutual understanding and peaceful means," he said.
The chief minister also appealed to people on both sides of the border not to allow the recent developments to affect the long-standing ties between the two states.
"I appeal to the people of both Assam and Arunachal Pradesh to maintain peace, harmony and mutual respect. Let us not allow differences to overshadow the strong bonds that unite our people," he said.
"Let us not allow differences to overshadow the strong bonds that unite our people," Khandu added.

LONDON , Aug. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Colebrook Bosson Saunders (CBS) recently launched its 2026 Sustainability Report, detailing progress against its 2030 sustainability targets spanning carbon reduction, circular design, material transparency, packaging, supplier engagement and community impact.
The report, the company's second annual, tracks performance against its 14 sustainability targets across three pillars: environmental stewardship, human health and well-being, and leading credentials and transparency.
Carbon reduction
CBS cut its total carbon emissions by 8.06% against its FY2023 baseline in the year to May 2025 (FY2025). Scope 1 and 2 emissions, which cover CBS's own operations, dropped 87.8% over the same period following a shift to renewable energy procurement, bringing electricity emissions to zero on a market basis.
Scope 3 emissions, those generated across the company's supply chain, which account for more than 99% of its total carbon footprint, fell 7.47% against the FY2023 baseline and 26% in a single year (FY2025). The reductions came largely from increased use of recycled content in products and lower embodied carbon across key top-selling products.
CBS has mapped the carbon footprint of 100% of its top-selling products, representing 80% of net sales in the year to May 2025, meeting that part of its 2026 target ahead of schedule. Coverage across the broader portfolio reached 97%, up from 74% the prior year. Flo and Flo Modular, two of CBS's best-selling monitor arms, each cut their lifecycle carbon footprint by 33% against the FY2023 baseline. Ollin followed with a 19% reduction in its product carbon footprint against the FY2023 baseline.
Circular design and packaging
As part of its mission to design out waste and keep materials in use for longer, CBS's top-selling products are made with recyclable materials, some by design from the outset, others through an active phase-out of harder-to-recycle plastics. By net sales, 98% of the broader portfolio was made with recyclable materials in FY2025. Among the changes, the company replaced harder-to-recycle plastics with polypropylene across key lines. The widely recyclable alternative makes products easier to disassemble and recover at end of life.
The company also partnered with refurbishment firms in the U.K., Asia, Australia and the Middle East to collect, refurbish and recirculate used products to support more sustainable end-of-life pathways and circular reuse.
Circularity extends beyond the product itself and into how it reaches the customer. Since introducing bulk packaging in 2022, CBS has expanded the format across multiple product lines. Bulk packaging options for the Flo Monitor Arm, which consolidate 10 units per pack, reduce packaging volume by 40.4% per unit. In the year to May 2025, 99.8% of products were delivered in plastic-free packaging using recyclable and biodegradable paper-based materials, based on net sales.
Sustainability credentials and material transparency
In 2026, CBS was awarded a Diamond climate strategy rating by Greenly, the carbon accounting platform's highest recognition, ranking CBS among the top 1% of more than 3,500 organisations it has assessed.
The company holds ISO 14001 and SCS Indoor Advantage Gold certification, verifying its products meet stringent indoor air quality standards. CBS aligns with science-based emissions targets as part of the MillerKnoll collective, which holds a Gold Medal from EcoVadis, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed globally for environmental performance.
CBS strengthened material transparency across its portfolio, with verified material ingredient labels supporting sustainable building standards, covering 94.4% of products by net sales. PFAS elimination remains a significant challenge across the manufacturing sector, but CBS has made a firm commitment to phase them out through ongoing material development. All products launched since March 2025 are free from intentionally added PFAS, excluding electronic parts. Remaining legacy material and product inventory is being responsibly phased out throughout 2026 and 2027.
Human health and well-being
CBS hosted more than 70 ergonomic education events in the year to May 2025, reaching 3,000 professionals across 14 countries. Associate participation in the company's annual Day of Purpose volunteering initiative rose to 85% from 75% the prior year.
"We believe high-performing, beautifully designed products and genuine sustainability progress are not mutually exclusive," said Andy Humphreys, managing director. "This year's report shows that when the whole business pulls in the same direction, the progress is real."
CBS was founded in London in 1990 and designs, manufactures and distributes ergonomic workplace products worldwide. It is an independent brand within the MillerKnoll collective.
The 2026 Sustainability Report is available at CBS's website. The company will continue working towards its 2030 targets across all three pillars of its sustainability framework.

Opinion Best of Both Sides: Student politics must serve campus, not disrupt it
Constructive student politics does not diminish the capacity to question, criticise or seek reform. It refines and elevates that capacity by embedding it within practices of responsibility and mutual respect
By Yogesh Singh
The conferment of the 2026 Dirac Medal, one of Physics’ highest honours, upon Padma Bhushan professor Deepak Dhar is the fruit of nearly four decades of dedicated research in Indian institutions. It illustrates the conditions under which sustained scholarly excellence becomes possible. Stable, disruption-free academic environments enable the continuity and collaborative depth required for work of this calibre. Such environments are not merely administrative preferences. They constitute the necessary foundation for the development of genuine knowledge and intellectual confidence among successive generations of university students.
This intellectual confidence has long found expression in the distinctive place students have occupied in the nation’s public life. From active participation in the freedom struggle to mobilisation during the Emergency and engagement with a range of contemporary social and political questions, students have consistently contributed to broader national conversations.
Yet the quality of that engagement depends heavily on how student representation is organised. When it is conducted with academic seriousness, transparency and a clear separation from external political interference, it becomes a genuine school of democratic responsibility. Age-appropriate eligibility, insistence on regular attendance, academic integrity and modest campaign practices help ensure that leadership emerges from all sections of society.
The decision to hold student elections across universities and colleges in Madhya Pradesh offers an opportunity to demonstrate that electoral processes on campus can be conducted with seriousness, modest means, transparent rules and a clear focus on the welfare of the students. When elections train young people in organisation, public speaking, coalition-building, graceful acceptance of outcomes and the responsible exercise of authority, they strengthen both democratic habits and the institutional culture on which genuine rights depend. It is only when students embrace their duties towards the institution and their peers that their rights to representation and voice acquire lasting legitimacy and effectiveness.
Student politics, at its best, is a training ground for discussion, debate and the establishment of responsible narratives. A university campus exists to nurture holistic development, compassionate thinking and a mindset that places the national interest and the pursuit of knowledge above factional advantage. When student leadership embraces this purpose, politics ceases to be a source of disruption and becomes a force for institutional strengthening.
The question that follows is how this ideal of responsible, institution-strengthening student leadership can be translated into concrete practice. A constructive, duty-oriented approach to student politics in universities and colleges would prioritise initiatives that strengthen the academic and social fabric of campuses. Campaigns focused on peer-study groups, research mentoring and support for learners can expand opportunity while raising overall standards.
Cultural and educational efforts, through students’ organisations, against ragging, emphasising respect, inclusion and institutional belonging offer more durable solutions than purely punitive measures alone. Student unions can be a meaningful tool in cleanliness and sustainability drives, cultivating habits of shared responsibility for the physical environment.
Structured peer mentoring programmes help newer students navigate academic and personal challenges. Regular, well-prepared debates and seminars on national and global issues provide forums for reasoned argument. Such activities train students in evidence-based discussion, listening, skills essential both to scholarship and to democratic citizenship.
Engagement with university administrations through data-backed proposals and sustained dialogue tends to produce more durable outcomes. Success, in this framework, can be measured by concrete improvements such as an enhanced academic atmosphere, stronger institutional standing and greater student participation in knowledge production. These metrics align student leadership with the long-term interests of students and with the wider goals of higher education.
In a diverse country like India, such processes also offer space for inclusive participation that reflects the social composition of the student body and contributes to national integration. More broadly, the cultivation of constructive student politics holds implications for the higher-education ecosystem and for national development. Institutions that combine intellectual freedom with disciplined environments are better positioned to produce researchers capable of original contributions, professionals equipped for complex problem-solving and citizens prepared for democratic participation.
Constructive student politics does not diminish the capacity to question, criticise or seek reform. It refines and elevates that capacity by embedding it within practices of responsibility and mutual respect. Campuses oriented toward academic excellence, civic discipline and reasoned engagement, where student leadership balances legitimate demands with a strong sense of duty, become fertile ground for the broader social, scientific and democratic progress that India seeks.
The achievements of scholars such as professor Dhar demonstrate that our campuses can generate work of global significance when conditions favour sustained inquiry. Expanding this possibility requires deliberate attention to the quality of campus culture, one in which student leadership itself becomes a partner in sustaining the conditions for excellence.
The writer is vice-chancellor, Delhi University

Amid the Opposition’s allegations that the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala was toeing the Sangh Parivar’s line after the Chief Secretary’s directive to government departments to ensure the recital of ‘Vande Mataram’ in its entirety during the Independence Day celebrations, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has said the State government has “its own stand on the issue, which will be clear to everyone on Independence Day”.
Speaking to the media after the Cabinet meeting on Thursday (August 13, 2026), Mr. Satheesan did not explicitly state that Vande Mataram will not be sung in its entirety, though press persons raised questions on the confusion that has arisen due to the Chief Secretary’s directive.
Instructions were reportedly issued in some schools and institutions mandating that the song be sung in full.
“The Chief Secretary’s directions were related to the Union government’s Har Ghar Tiranga campaign. The Parliament has now passed a Bill making intentional insult to Vande Mataram a punishable offence with jail term up to three years. It mandates that the song be sung in full. The President has also given assent to the Act. However, the Congress-led UDF has a clear stand on this. We will act only as per that,” he said.
As per the directive signed by Chief Secretary Bishwanath Sinha on August 6, the Union Ministry of Culture had on July 14, 2026 communicated that the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign will be observed this year from August 9 to 17. The campaign has been integrated with the third phase of the nationwide commemoration of the 150 years of Vande Mataram. Accordingly, all physical celebrations during this period have to combine the collective singing of Vande Mataram with the hoisting of the national flag.
The letter further states that the “instructions of the Government of India for recitation of Vande Mataram will be followed in full”.
The Local Self-Government department and the General Education Department are the nodal departments for the programme. However, an earlier circular issued by the General Administration Department on August 4 does not make any mention of Vande Mataram recital as part of Independence Day celebrations.
Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan had said that singing the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram was not wrong, but the song in its entirety went against the secular spirit of the country, which was the opinion of the Constituent Assembly also. The later stanzas of the song refer to deities of a specific religion.

Sri Lankan refugees in Tamil Nadu can return home: What are the conditions?
The move comes months after former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin wrote a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking Centre's intervention on several issues faced by Sri Lankan Tamils living in India for more than four decades.
4 min readNew DelhiUpdated: Aug 13, 2026 03:36 PM IST
Former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin had earlier urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to intervene on issues faced by Sri Lankan Tamils living in India. (AI-generated image)
Sri Lanka’s Cabinet has approved special arrangements to facilitate the voluntary return of citizens who fled the country during the civil war and have been living in India without valid passports or after leaving through unauthorised ports, local media reported.
The move follows the advice of the Attorney General to provide necessary immigration clearance facilities for Sri Lankan refugees seeking to voluntarily return to the country through the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the report stated.
According to his letter, around 89,000 refugees reside in and outside camps across Tamil Nadu, with nearly 40% of them having been born in India.
What are the conditions for return?
According to the Cabinet’s decision, Sri Lankans who left the country between August 1, 2006 and May 19, 2009, without using an approved port or possessing valid travel documents, will be required to obtain a clearance report.
This report will be issued by the State Intelligence Service after verifying the refugees’ identities as Sri Lankan citizens through Sri Lankan diplomatic missions in India.
The process will also provide the returnees with clearance from involvement in murder, treason, and other offences under specific legal provisions, Ada Derana reported.

Those found to have committed or been involved in these offences will be detained at the port of entry and handed over to the relevant authorities for further legal action, a statement by the Sri Lankan Department of Government Information highlighted.
Those who receive clearance will be issued temporary passports and allowed to enter Sri Lanka through an authorised port without being prosecuted under the relevant provisions of the Immigrants and Emigrants Act No. 20 of 1948, according to the government statement.
A mechanised boat, which belonged to local fishermen, Wellington, was also seized, according to the report.

This was the third boat captured by the Sri Lankan Navy within a span of one and a half months, Saveriyar Fishermen Association President Sagayam Saveriyar said, expressing deep concern over detentions.

Out of more than 600 mechanised boats operating from Rameswaram, only over 300 ventured into the sea on August 12 amid persistent fears of seizures by the Sri Lankan Navy, local fisherfolk told PTI.
Sagayam Saveriyar told PTI, “The Sri Lankan Navy intercepted the boat and arrested nine fishermen. It is distressing that both the Central and State governments are remaining indifferent to this issue.”
The president also sought urgent intervention of the Central and state governments to secure prompt releases of the fishermen and their vessels.

He warned that the fishing community would be forced to begin protests if swift steps were not taken.
The association leader also stated that while the current Tamil Nadu government under Joseph Vijay had promised to resolve the Sri Lankan maritime issue, detentions have continued unabated, the news agency quoted.
He called on authorities to intervene and ensure that fishermen are allowed to carry out traditional fishing activities in the Katchatheevu region without harassment.
The developments are significant for Tamil Nadu because thousands of Sri Lankan Tamils have lived in the state for decades, while arrests of Indian fishermen by Sri Lankan authorities remain a recurring source of tension between New Delhi and Colombo.

Din, disruptions and a dozen bills: Monsoon Session comes to a close
The disruptions had two key flashpoints. One was the police crackdown on students at Jantar Mantar and the other was the alleged theft of Ram Temple donations.
Parliament's 25-day monsoon session ended in acrimony on Thursday, with both Houses adjourned sine die after a stretch that saw proceedings disrupted almost daily, with Lok Sabha going without a completed Question Hour on even a single sitting day.
The disruptions had two key flashpoints. One was the July 20 police crackdown on students protesting at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak — an episode that led to Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation as Union education minister, and that the opposition wanted Union home minister Amit Shah to explain in the House.
The other was a running opposition allegation of theft of donations collected at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.
The Lok Sabha played all six stanzas of the national song Vande Mataram soon after convening on Thursday, after which speaker Om Birla adjourned the House sine die. He skipped the traditional valedictory address, which typically highlights the session's performance and productivity. The Congress, the Samajwadi Party and the Trinamool Congress boycotted the customary meeting with Birla thereafter.
Also Read | Lok Sabha Om Birla urges Opposition to end Parliament logjam
The Rajya Sabha was also adjourned sine die, ending the session. Chairman CP Radhakrishnan expressed "deep concern" over disruptions that "derailed" the business of the House. Overall, the Lok Sabha functioned for 17.5 hours while the Rajya Sabha worked for 37.4 hours.
Jantar Mantar crackdown dominates session
The session was dominated by a showdown between the Opposition and the Centre over the former's demand for a debate and a statement by Shah on the police crackdown on protesting students at Delhi's Jantar Mantar last month, which led to the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.
On the penultimate day, the Centre's push for a debate failed as the Opposition rejected Shah's offer of a two-day discussion on the NEET paper leak and other issues, followed by a reply from him. "The Centre is ready for discussions. The House should be allowed to run, the Opposition should submit a letter to the speaker by 2pm today. We are ready to start discussion at 3pm today," Shah told reporters outside Parliament on Wednesday.
Also Read | Rijiju defends Shah amid Oppn persistent demand for HM’s statement
He also wrote to Birla conveying the government's readiness to participate in the discussion. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called it a “last-minute attempt” and said the Opposition was not interested in listening to Shah’s lecture.
The bills Parliament dealt with
Despite repeated disruptions and protests inside and outside Parliament, both Houses tabled and in some cases, passed a series of bills.
Foreign contribution bill referred to JPC after Opposition, church pushback
A bill proposing contentious changes to India's foreign contribution law was referred to a 31-member joint parliamentary committee (JPC) amid a standoff between the government and the Opposition, and repeated disruptions in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.
Among the key concerns are a plan to empower a "designated authority" to take over, manage or sell assets built with foreign funds by non-governmental organisations whose licences are cancelled, suspended or not renewed.
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill - it was introduced in the previous session but held back - drew objections from the Opposition, several church delegations and four chief ministers of Christian-majority states.
Minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai moved the resolution in the Lok Sabha to form the JPC, comprising 21 Lok Sabha members and 10 Rajya Sabha members. A BJP member is expected to head the panel. The Opposition, which had pushed the government to scrap the bill, said it would join the committee.
Centre, Opposition united over paper leak
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 — brought against the backdrop of protests by students after the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak — was the only legislation passed in both Houses after a full debate this session. The bill overhauls the 2024 law by introducing stricter jail terms, enhancing penalties, and setting timelines for probe and trial in fast-track courts.
According to PRS Legislative Research, the Lok Sabha spent over 10 hours discussing the bill and the Rajya Sabha over six hours. Opposition parties led by the Congress staged a walkout before the bill was passed in the Rajya Sabha, with leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge saying it was incomplete in its current form. Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the move.
"It is indeed an achievement to clear a number of bills with one week left in the session. But we should not be blamed for passing the bills amid din," a senior government functionary told HT on condition of anonymity.
New law brings banking records into the digital age
Both Houses passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, replacing a 135-year-old British-era statute with a framework that makes electronic, digital, virtual and cloud-stored bank records admissible and enforceable evidence in court.
The law it replaces, the Bankers' Books Evidence Act of 1891, was built for a world of physical ledgers, and was never designed for cloud-based, electronic, digital or other storage formats even after several amendments.
Delayed registration of births, deaths made more stringent
Parliament also passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, tightening one of India's oldest civil laws. The change is narrow on paper — a single sub-section of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 — but it re-routes how births and deaths reported more than two years late are registered.
Beyond that threshold, cases now go to a judicial magistrate of the first class, a judicial officer under the high court, instead of an executive magistrate, a district-cadre administrator under the state government.
This is the second time in three years that Parliament has amended a statute most people encounter only once — to prove they were born.
"The government wants that every child born in the country should be registered and every death should also be registered... Anyone who has died, cannot continue to remain in the voter lists to benefit some parties," minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai said.
Several members of the National Democratic Alliance backed the bill as necessary, while the Opposition pressed for Shah's presence in the House. CPI(M)'s AA Rahim, among those raising the demand, cited the deaths of more than 20 students linked to the NEET paper leak.
'Vande Mataram' gets legal protection on a par with national anthem
Both Houses cleared a bill giving Vande Mataram the same legal status as the national anthem — the first bill passed amid din this session. President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent on Tuesday.
The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 went through on a voice vote after 14 minutes of debate, with only three MPs — DMK's K Kanimozhi and A Raja, and BJP's Sambit Patra — speaking.
It makes insulting or obstructing the national song a criminal offence, punishable by up to three years in jail and a fine, extending protections currently reserved for the national flag, anthem and Constitution.
Patra said the timing coincided with Vande Mataram's 150th anniversary. The Opposition said nationalism cannot be legislated. The move follows the Centre's earlier decision making all six stanzas mandatory, departing from the two-stanza version adopted as the national song in 1950.
Sitharaman assures no UPI tax, but bill gives Centre power to redefine what stays free
Parliament passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, with finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman ruling out any tax on UPI. Digital payments stay free for consumers, she said.
Cleared by the Lok Sabha last week, the bill was passed in the Rajya Sabha by a voice vote after a brief debate and Sitharaman's reply. It severs the link between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the Income Tax Act, and gives the government legal backing to alter the zero-MDR framework for UPI and RuPay.
Banks and payment providers cannot currently charge users on UPI or RuPay debit transactions, directly or indirectly. The bill lets the Centre decide, by notification, which payment modes stay free.
Supreme Court judges to increase
Parliament also passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, raising the top court's sanctioned strength from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.
The bill, which replaced a May ordinance, received the President's assent on Tuesday and comes amid a mounting case backlog. It cleared on a voice vote as Opposition members walked out, with Union minister Arjun Ram Meghwal saying the government was committed to judicial independence.
Kerala set for a new name: Keralam
Kerala will soon be known as Keralam. The Rajya Sabha passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, by voice vote on Wednesday, a day after the Lok Sabha cleared it.
"The bill provides that the State of Kerala will be known as the State of Keralam," Rai said. The Constitution's First Schedule will be amended under Article 3 to reflect the new name.
Parliament clips states' powers to tax minerals
Parliament also passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, curbing states' powers to tax mineral rights and "mineral-bearing lands". The bill went through on a voice vote, without debate, amid Opposition protests.
A new section bars states from imposing "any tax, cess or such other levy (by whatever name called)" on mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands — whether linked to mineral quantity, value or royalty — unless the central government prescribes otherwise. It will take effect once the President gives assent.
Parliament passes bill to fix delayed payments to MSMEs
Parliament passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, aimed at the long-standing problem of delayed payments to MSMEs. The bill seeks to improve the sector's administrative structure and streamline payment mechanisms.

Congress slams ‘havan’ after Kharge’s Uttarakhand rally, BJP denies link
Khajan Das, Uttarakhand Minister and a Dalit leader from the BJP, said the party had no connection to the “purification” programme and the organisation behind it.
A ‘purification’ ritual organised in Uttarakhand’s Haldwani after a visit by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge last week has sparked a political row ahead of the Assembly polls. While the Congress has alleged that those who organised the ‘shuddhikaran havan’ were linked to the BJP and said it reflected a casteist mindset, the ruling party has distanced itself from the event. Kharge, too, has spoken up. Raising the issue in Rajya Sabha, he said he had never asked anyone to protect him because he is a Dalit, but the ‘purification’ event made him feel humiliated.
Kharge addressed a public meeting at Ram Lila ground in Nainital district on August 8. Two days later, an organisation, Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas, performed a “shuddhikaran havan” at the ground.
Criticising the event, state Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal said, “The ‘purification’ of the platform from which the AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge ji addressed the public during the Congress rally in Haldwani, performed by individuals associated with the BJP, is extremely hurtful and reprehensible.” “This incident reflects the caste-based discrimination and narrow-minded mentality of those in the BJP. The Congress believes in humanity, equality, and brotherhood, whereas such events promote hatred and division in society,” he said. Godiyal urged the police to take note and ensure proper action against the guilty.
Congress also said that the BJP was in a state of panic after the success of Kharge’s rally. He said that by performing the “shuddhikaran havan” and sprinkling gangajal at Ram Lila ground, people of the ruling party displayed their “anti-Dalit” mindset.
Speaking to The Indian Express, Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas president Girish Chandra Pandey denied any association with the BJP and RSS. He said that ‘havan’ was performed because the Hindu community’s sentiments were hurt when Kharge called Hindu organisations a “snake” and used a Hindu cultural site in Haldwani for a political purpose. Pandey confirmed that he was referring to Kharge’s remark during the Assam poll campaign earlier this year in which he described the ideology of the RSS and BJP as a “venomous snake”. “We also wanted to make an appeal that the venue meant for cultural activities not be used for political programmes,” he said.
Rejecting the Congress’s allegations that an “anti-Dalit” mindset was behind the ‘purification’ ritual, Pandey said four Dalits were among those who performed the ‘havan’. Pandey said he founded this organisation only three months ago to spread religious and social awareness.
BJP denies link
Khajan Das, a state Cabinet Minister and a Dalit leader from the BJP, said the party had no connection to the “purification” programme and the organisation behind it. “Hindu religious programmes are organised at Ram Lila ground. But slogans of another community were raised during the Congress rally. That hurts the Hindu community,” Das told The Indian Express. He said Congress has raked up the caste issue only for a political purpose. The minister added, “Congress pretends to be a well-wisher of Dalits, but has always insulted Dalit leaders such as BR Ambedkar and Babu Jagjivan Ram.”

The State government has entered into an understanding with IIT-Madras for protection of the Uppada coast in Kakinada district.
As a part of it, a seawall will be constructed there under the expert guidance of IIT-Madras, which will prepare the DPR and also monitor the project implementation, which is scheduled to commence in November.
Kakinada District Collector M.N. Harendhira Prasad and IIT-Madras Ocean Engineering Department professor S.A. Sannasiraj inked the pact in the presence of Deputy Chief Minister and Minister for Environment & Forests K. Pawan Kalyan, at his camp office, near Mangalagiri, on Wednesday.
An official release said the seawall would be built at an approximate cost of ₹323 crore and the State Disaster Management Authority would act as the nodal agency for the project being taken up with the approval of the National Disaster Management Authority.
The AP Maritime Board (APMB) would be the executive agency and IIT-Madras would prepare the design on the basis of a comprehensive study of the intensity of the coastal erosion at Uppada, ocean currents and action of the waves to be done by it.
AP Pollution Control Board Member-Secretary S. Sri Saravanan, Pithapuram Area Development Authority Director N.V. Sivaram Prasad, SDMA Executive Director Khateeb Kouser Bano, and APMB Chief Engineer G.V. Raghava Rao were present.

The long-delayed Joka-Esplanade metro in Kolkata has seen a breakthrough as the final lap of tunneling work was completed on Tuesday (August 11, 2026). This is the second and final tunnel in this line, the previous one had reached completion on July 10.
Also read | Railways to invest ₹1 lakh crore in upgrading infrastructure in West Bengal
The Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) ‘Divya’ successfully achieved breakthrough at Victoria Metro Station around Tuesday (August 11) noon. Just a month back, TBM ‘Durga’ had already achieved breakthrough for the first tunnel at the same station.
Two TBMs are being used for construction of twin tube tunnels from Khidderpore to Park Street, beyond which tunnelling will be done by conventional Cut & Cover method.
The Joka-Esplanade metro is the Purple line, and once completely operational, it will help add to the network of metro lines in the city, improving the public transport system of West Bengal’s capital. Currently, the Blue and Green metro lines in Kolkata are completely operational, and the Purple and Orange lines have truncated services due to delay in construction work and unfinished lines.
Speaking on the occasion of TBM Divya’s final tunnel drilling process, Prem Sagar Gupta, General Manager, Metro Railway, Kolkata, appreciated the commitment and teamwork of the project personnel who ensured safe, systematic and efficient tunnelling while maintaining the highest standards of quality and safety, without disturbing the surface traffic and normal activities in this densely populated part of the city.
The initial construction work for this line started in 2011 and has seen several delays and obstructions during the construction work.
TBM Durga started boring the 1.75 km tunnel between Kidderpore and Victoria in July 2025, and TBM Divya started the work on October 2025.
The Purple line is currently working on an 8km stretch above the surface between Joka and Majerhat stations. The entire project is expected to be operational in 2029.

A parliamentary panel has flagged a "drastic decline" in the number of schools and students as education level rises, noting that nearly 73% students drop out before finishing higher secondary.
The recommendation is part of the Tenth Report (Eighteenth Lok Sabha) of the Committee on Estimates (2026-27) on "Budget and Policy aspects for providing Affordable and Quality Education in the Country including Review of Central Board of Secondary Education", presented to Lok Sabha on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).
The committee noted that the number of schools at Secondary and Higher Secondary levels are very less when compared with the number of schools at Primary and Upper Primary levels.
It said as per the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) 2024-25, out of the total 10,92,671 schools, including all the government and government aided schools, there are 9,11,032 schools at primary level, 4,12,805 schools at upper primary level, 1,61,808 schools at secondary level, and only 90,866 schools at higher secondary level in the country.
With regard to the number of students enrolled, in primary classes there are 6,18,45,033 students and 4,08,93,978 students in upper primary classes from 6 to 8, which reduces to 2,36,68,220 in secondary, and further reduces to 1,64,17,949 in higher secondary classes.
Drastic decline in number of schools
"The committee are concerned to note this drastic decline in number of schools and students as education levels rises," it said.
"From the above information, the Committee note that out of over 1 million (10 lakhs) government schools, the vast majority are only primary schools, and nearly 73% of students drop out before finishing higher secondary," it added.
The committee strongly urged the Ministry to prioritise upgrading existing primary and secondary schools into full higher secondary schools to ensure a high school is physically accessible to students belonging to different communities and to arrest student drop-off rate.
"The Committee are of the view that there is an urgent need to increase the number of schools at secondary and higher secondary levels," it said.
Considering that education is placed in the Concurrent List of the Constitution with most schools under the jurisdiction of the State Governments and UT Administration, the committee desired the Ministry to impress upon all the State/UT Government to take steps for setting up of more secondary and higher secondary schools so as to increase the enrolment of students in the country.
Gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure
On facilities for Divyang students to achieve inclusive education across the country, the committee flagged a severe gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure, noting that more than half of schools across the country are devoid of CwSN-friendly infrastructure.
The committee noted that in order to achieve the objective of inclusive education, the Ministry of Education provides financial support to State Governments and Union Territories to strengthen infrastructure and human resources for inclusive education of Divyang students under the Samagra Shiksha scheme.
To improve physical accessibility of schools, the scheme includes specific provisions for the creation of barrier-free and differently-abled-friendly infrastructure, such as ramps, handrails and accessible toilets, so that children with disabilities can move safely and participate fully in school activities.
Though the committee appreciated the vision of the Ministry, it noted that as per UDISE+ 2024-25, out of total 14,71,437 schools at national level, only 5,23,143 schools have CwSN (Children with special needs) toilets, and only 8,08,466 schools have ramps with handrails.
During 2024-25, a budget of ₹482 lakh was allocated for construction of 186 CwSN toilets, however only ₹2.60 lakh was actually utilised with no progress in physical targets.
"The severe gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure shows that more than half of the schools across the country are devoid of CwSN friendly infrastructure," the committee said.
The committee further noted that under the financial support for new special educators, only ₹80.50 lakh was utilised against a budgetary grant (elementary section) of ₹962 lakh.
It also noted that a meagre progress was achieved in the area of recruiting/retaining special educators for CwSN students.
On the Ministry's approach to promoting education for Divyang children, the committee noted that it is rights based, inclusive and holistic.
It said The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPnD) Act, 2016 provides that children with benchmark disabilities are entitled to free education up to the age of 18 years.
The NEP 2020 emphasises a Zero Rejection Policy for children with disabilities, ensuring that no child is denied schooling on account of disability. The policy also underscores the importance of preparing and training teachers to handle inclusive classrooms effectively, it said.
"In view of the above, the Committee strongly recommend the Ministry to adhere to yearly targets of budget utilisation and execution of CwSN related projects in a time bound manner," it said.
The committee recommended the Ministry provide safe and accessible infrastructure to Divyang students in a time-bound manner to achieve the objective of inclusivity in education.
The Ministry should also assess the requirement of special educators across the country and complete their recruitment at the earliest, it said.

The Supreme Court on Thursday (August 13, 2026) agreed to confront the Centre, Delhi Police Commissioner with questions raised by Rajya Sabha Member of Parliament A.A. Rahim moved the Supreme Court on the deployment of facial recognition technology and allied mass-surveillance measures against students and persons who participated in the Cockroach Janta Party-linked protests over the NEET-UG exam paper leaks.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy and advocate Subhash Chandran that Mr. Rahim’s petition would be tagged with the main NEET-UG protest petitions, which have questioned the police crackdown on students and the use of pellet guns.
Ms. Guruswamy submitted that the surveillance was done by the police on the ground and the data was hosted with private agencies.
“One maps your face. Spectacles are used and a vehicle is also used. The data is taken without permission. Then private entities host the data in violation of DPDP Rules, CrPC and a variety of things,” Ms. Guruswamy submitted.
The MP said that the use of facial recognition technology and covert surveillance on peaceful protesters was unconstitutional.
“The gravamen of the challenge is the automated, algorithmic extraction and matching of the biometric identifiers of thousands of peaceful protesters, and the interlinking of such data with permanent national criminal databases. Since the commencement of the sit-in on July 20, the Delhi Police have subjected thousands of protesters, journalists and ordinary citizens to continuous and pervasive biometric surveillance,” the petition said.

The plea said the surveillance was done through the acquisition of videos and photographs through CCTV cameras, drones, a mobile command and control vehicle and hand-held devices.
“The real-time processing of such footage through automated facial recognition technology using the ‘Ikshana’ vehicle and ‘AjnaLens’ smart spectacles and the collection and matching of fingerprints through the National Crime Records Bureau’s ‘Abhigyan’ mobile application against the National Automated Fingerprint Identification System. This surveillance was carried out in a complete legal vacuum,” the petition said.
The plea said neither the Delhi Police’s own standing orders governing protests nor the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022 authorise the biometric surveillance of persons attending a lawful assembly.

A system brewing in the north Bay of Bengal, adjoining the West Bengal-Bangladesh coasts, is likely to bring light to moderate rainfall in Andhra Pradesh through this week.
According to the 8.30 a.m. bulletin from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, a low-pressure area that formed on August 12 intensified into a well-marked low-pressure area at around 5.30 a.m. on Thursday (August 13, 2026). It is likely to continue moving north-westwards across Gangetic West Bengal towards Jharkhand, and may concentrate into a depression by Thursday evening.
Under the influence of the system, coastal areas in the State may receive light to moderate showers and thunderstorms until August 16. Isolated strong surface winds, with speeds reaching 40-50 kmph, are likely across the State this week.
The A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) has said thunderstorms and rainfall are likely at a few stations on Thursday. As of 11 a.m., no station other than Kadiri in Sri Sathya Sai district and Peddapuram in Kakinada district had recorded any major rainfall. Kadiri and Peddapuram received light rain of around 11 mm each.
After a dry July, the State has received about-normal rainfall since August 1. It has not been enough to bring down the overall deficit, which stands at 50.6%.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Thursday (August 13, 2026) inaugurated the second phase of the Seed Access Road (E-3), along with two steel bridges, at Undavalli, describing the development as the first major step towards building the capital city.
Mr. Naidu unveiled the plaque at Undavalli to mark the inauguration and addressed a public meeting attended by Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana, Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar, APCRDA Commissioner V. Vijay Rama Raju, MLAs Tenali Sravan Kumar and Kolikapudi Srinivas, MP Bhashyam Ramakrishna, farmers and residents.
The Seed Access Road has been completed from Rayapudi through Venkatapalem, Penumaka and Undavalli. The project, developed at an estimated cost of ₹1,519 crore, is planned for expansion in its third phase to connect the capital region with National Highway 16 near Manipal. The bridges will improve connectivity between Vijayawada, Mangalagiri and Amaravati.
The two steel bridges are a 110-metre structure across the Buckingham Canal and a 280-metre bridge across the Kondaveeti Vagu and the Guntur Channel. Mr. Naidu walked some distance down the bridges, inspecting the construction.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Naidu recalled that farmers had contributed about 34,000 acres for the capital, and paid tribute to those who gave their lands. He said the capital’s development had been disrupted during the previous government, forcing the present government to close contracts, retender works and restart construction.
Mr. Naidu said Singapore had supported the Amaravati master plan and Norman Foster’s London-based firm had been engaged for the iconic government buildings. He rejected criticism that Amaravati was merely a “graphics” project, saying the vision was becoming reality.
He said Amaravati would be developed as a pollution-free deep-tech capital, with AI and quantum-computing hubs, with the aim of placing it among India’s top five cities. He said the capital region would cover Amaravati, Mangalagiri, Tadepalli, Guntur and Vijayawada, and that the Centre had sanctioned a 190-km outer ring road and a 96-km inner ring road.
The project also envisages underground utility corridors for electricity, gas, telephone and water services across Amaravati. Mr. Naidu said Amaravati would be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2028 as a capital admired by the country. Calling the Seed Access Road and the steel bridges the first step, he urged people to contribute ideas and work towards making Andhra Pradesh a “Swarna Andhra” by 2047.

In a fresh incident, 10 fishermen from Rameswaram in Tamil Nadu were arrested by Sri Lankan Navy personnel on charges of poaching in international waters late on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) night.
The Fisheries Department officials on Thursday (August 13) said that they had issued 297 tokens to mechanised trawlers on Wednesday morning from the Rameswaram jetty.
At around 10 p.m. on Wednesday, a boat belonging to Wellington of Rajan Nagar, Thangachimadam, was intercepted reportedly by the Sri Lankan Navy’s surveillance team at the Katchatheevu islet. After preliminary inquiry, the Navy personnel took the fishermen, including Janathan (45), Antony Pitchai (38), Prabhu (43), Don Bosco (55), Arockia devin (31), Veluchamy (51), Subbiah (52), Arockia Jeniston (25), and Stevin (30), into custody. The arrested fishermen hailed from Rameswaram, Pamban, Virudhunagar, and Thangachimadam.
A senior official in the Tamil Nadu Fisheries Department said that the arrested fishermen were taken to Talaimannar Naval Port and are likely to be produced in a court during the day.
Meanwhile, fishermen in the coastal district were distressed by the news. One fisherman said, “Only five days ago, we had stayed away from fishing for a day following the arrest of nine fishermen after their trawler reportedly developed a technical snag near Neduntheevu islet...”
“The latest arrest shows that the Centre and the Tamil Nadu government were only mute spectators and don’t seem to be interested in finding a lasting solution. When we have been appealing repeatedly to help and intervene as it involved our livelihood, such a nonchalant attitude had caused hardships and mental agony among our families,” Jesu Raja, a fisherman leader, told The Hindu.

There ends a legal drama with all the ingredients of a fascinating crime thriller: a prime 12-acre vacant plot worth unofficially over Rs 100 crore in eastern Bengaluru, four different women claiming to be ‘Radha’, the widowed heir of the late original owner, and a top real estate executive caught right in the crosshairs.
The case involved alleged forgery of a gift deed in the name of one Radha, who died before the date of the deed; a gift deed by another Radha to her children; and a third woman named Radha with a daughter, apart from a childless woman who filed a police complaint claiming to be the actual heir.
Now, after months of investigation untangling a web of forgery and identity theft, the Bengaluru police have finally identified the real widow and communicated their intent to file a closure report to the Karnataka High Court on August 3.
Reporting its findings to Justice M I Arun, the police confirmed that the genuine owner is the second Radha, who legitimately inherited the Bandapura village land following her husband S Krishnan’s death in 1986. Her children, having received the property through valid gift deeds, subsequently executed a joint development agreement and general power of attorney with Sattva Group.
The police informed the court that Ashwin Sancheti, senior executive at Sattva Group, who was previously arrested and released on bail, is completely innocent of any wrongdoing.
“After the investigation, the state is of the opinion that petitioner no.2 (Radha) is the legally wedded wife of late S Krishnan, who owned the property and petitioner nos. 3, 4 and 5 are their children,” the High Court noted while recording the police investigation details.
“That petitioner no.1 (Sancheti), who represents a limited company, got a joint development agreement and the general power of Attorney executed from petitioner nos. 2 to 5 to develop the property, which is the subject matter of the writ petition and that he had no role in executing any other documents pertaining to the ownership of the property,” the High Court added.
The court also noted that the probe revealed that the woman who filed the original FIR alleging fraud was herself an impostor named Chaitra, acting alongside a general power of attorney holder to grab the multi-crore land parcel illegally.
The court directed the initiation of proceedings against the complainant, who claimed to be the real Radha through a general power of attorney holder identified as K Venkatappa, 65.
After the police report was submitted, the complainant stated that four different people were falsely claiming to be her in an attempt to usurp her property. She insisted that she is “the true Radha” and maintained that her complaint is legitimate. She also said she would contest the police’s closure report for the case before the magistrate.
Justice M I Arun directed the Avalahalli jurisdiction police to file the closure report and that the trial court should process the same in accordance with law and pass appropriate orders thereafter.
The dispute centres on 12 acres and 30.5 guntas of open land in eastern Bengaluru. The matter escalated in October 2025 when an FIR was registered based on allegations from a woman claiming to be the childless, sole surviving spouse of Krishnan. She accused Sancheti and others of using forged documents and impersonation to usurp the property.
According to the complaint filed by the 65-year-old woman, through a general power of attorney, she is the absolute owner of the land in Bandapura and was shocked when she went to inspect her property and found that someone else was in possession and its nature had been changed.
According to the complaint, the land was purchased by her husband Krishnan with a registered sale deed dated October 6, 1978, which is in her possession, and her husband died on May 29, 1986. After her husband’s death, her name was reportedly entered in the revenue records since she did not have children, and she was in possession of the land.
The police case was challenged in the High Court by Sancheti, whose firm signed the joint development agreement worth over Rs 20 crore for the disputed property with the real heir Radha’s children.
The Karnataka High Court in January this year ruled that the case involves “matters that cry out for investigation”. “To interdict such investigation at the threshold would be to prematurely close the doors of criminal justice and to permit serious allegations of fraud to go unanswered,” Justice M Nagaprasanna ruled on January 20.
The High Court then pointed out that the case is not confined to rival claims over land titles but “traverses far deeper, into the realm of deceit, impersonation, forgery and calculated fraud”.
